title: Healthy lifestyle choices

accuracy.evidence: Checked on 24 Nov 2026: 60 minutes a day on average for ages 5-18 against the UK Chief Medical Officers' Physical Activity Guidelines 2019; the talk test against NHS 'Exercise'; free-sugar limits 19 g (4-6), 24 g (7-10), 30 g (11+), the 150 ml juice cap, whole fruit and plain milk not counting, and 35 g in a 330 ml can of cola against NHS 'How to cut down on sugar' and 'Sugar: the facts'; acid attack of up to an hour per intake against the Oral Health Foundation; CO binding haemoglobin about 210 times more tightly than oxygen (Blumenthal 2001, J R Soc Med) and smokers' COHb of 3-10%, up to 15% in heavy smokers (RIVM 2021; Gloucestershire NHS pathology reference ranges), which the lab's 1 seat in 10 matches; sleep 9-12 h for ages 6-12 against AASM (Paruthi 2016). The lab's 84 to 78 resting rate and 50 to 54 ml stroke volume are labelled as example values and keep cardiac output near 4.2 L/min (84x50, 82x51, 80x53, 79x53, 78x54 worked by hand).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips for this Year 6 statement: exercise wears the heart out (step 2 predict and 'worn'), only one long session counts (step 3 predict and 'once'), exciting screen games count as activity (video game and TV cards are refused, 'sit'), juice is fine because it is fruit and whole fruit counts as free sugar (step 4 predict, 'juice' and 'fruit'), grazing sweets is kinder to teeth (step 5 predict and 'graze'), and smoking only harms the lungs ('lungs').

lab_distinct.evidence: Six mechanisms specific to lifestyle and body function: a run/rest loop that drives heart rate and breathing rate together and refuses rest before effort; an 8-week training calendar where resting rate falls while ml per beat rises; an activity picker that refuses sitting cards with the reason; a free-sugar budget that refuses any choice that would pass 24 g and explains why apple and milk add 0 g; a school-day timeline where acid hours equal the number of separate sugar times; and red blood cells whose oxygen seats are taken by carbon monoxide in smoky air. Gate measured under 30% overlap with every other flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is found by doing before the strip confirms it: the heart number climbs with every Run tap and only falls on Sit; the calendar blocks lower the resting rate one fortnight at a time; tapping Video game shows it adds no active minutes; adding cola is refused because 35 g alone passes the day's limit; spreading sweets across slots lights more acid teeth and the count of hours rises; smoky air leaves one cell with a grey CO seat and the oxygen count drops to 9 of 10.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'It goes up: the heart is worn out' (resting rate falls 84 to 78), 'Yes, or they do not count' (15+15+20+10 minute bursts reach 60), 'Yes, all sugar counts' (apple and milk add 0 g while juice adds 13 g), and 'One every hour: less sugar at a time' (four separate slots give up to 4 hours of acid against 1 hour at lunch).

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() gives a distinct message for each wrong tag across 8 challenge questions: up (muscles need more oxygen), worn (stronger heart, more blood per beat), sit (screen time is sitting time), once (short bursts add up), fruit (whole fruit and milk sugar are not free, juice is), juice (35 g cola against 24 g), graze (four sugar times, four attacks) and lungs (CO in the blood and a harder-working heart).

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text FK grade 2.5 and the adult text 9.1, inside the learner limits of 6.5 and 9.5. Kid sentences are short and concrete (puff, get warm, sugar inside a whole apple), technical words are introduced once with a meaning, and lab strips fit in two to three lines at 390 px.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph carries a mechanism or a number: oxygen and heart rate, stronger heart and 60 active minutes, free sugar and the 24 g limit with acid attacks, carbon monoxide, tar, alcohol and sleep hours. The adult text adds the NC statement, CMO guideline and talk test, NHS sugar limits and Oral Health Foundation timing, CO binding and sleep advice, then the common mistakes, without repeating any of it.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark themes at every step after Show me: the run and rest tiles fill the bottom row, the 4 training blocks sit in one row with readable labels (the resting-rate text was shortened after it clipped at 390 px), activity and food cards drop to 2 columns, the 8 time slots wrap to 2 rows of 4 with the tooth icons visible, and the 10 blood cells sit in 2 rows of 5. The button row below the canvas wraps.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a button twin: Run on the spot and Sit and rest, Add weeks, one button per remaining activity and food with its minutes or grams, one per time slot plus Clear the day, and Breathe clean or smoky air. note() updates the canvas aria-label and c.say() announces every result. walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13 with all 6 tasks completing via Show me, the challenge showing, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes and no console errors.

sources: UK Chief Medical Officers' Physical Activity Guidelines (2019)
NHS: Exercise (talk test for moderate and vigorous activity)
NHS: How to cut down on sugar in your diet; Sugar: the facts (free sugar limits by age, 150 ml juice cap)
Oral Health Foundation: Diet and my teeth (acid attack up to an hour after sugar)
Blumenthal I (2001) Carbon monoxide poisoning, J R Soc Med 94(6) (CO affinity about 210 times that of oxygen)
RIVM (2021) Carbon monoxide in tobacco smoke (COHb 3-8% in smokers, up to 15% in chain-smokers)
Paruthi S et al. (2016) Recommended amount of sleep for pediatric populations, J Clin Sleep Med 12(6)
UK Chief Medical Officer (2009) Guidance on the consumption of alcohol by children and young people
DfE (2013) National Curriculum science, Year 6 Animals including humans
